question_text:
Hermit crabs protect their soft bodies by living inside empty snail shells, and a crab that grows must eventually find a larger shell. On a rocky shore, researchers observed that crabs wearing shells too small for them almost always switched to a larger empty shell when one lay within a few inches. One crab, recently grown, was wearing a cramped shell, and a larger empty shell lay a few inches away. Given this pattern, the crab most likely ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: will stay in its cramped shell because the shell is familiar.
answer_b: will stop using shells and live without any protection.
answer_c: will leave the cramped shell and move into the larger one.
answer_d: will switch shells only if a predator forces it out.
explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it follows directly from the stated pattern. The text says that crabs in shells too small for them almost always switched to a larger empty shell when one was within a few inches. This crab has a cramped shell and a larger empty shell lies a few inches away, so the crab will most likely move into the larger shell.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It reverses the observed pattern. The text says crabs in shells that were too small almost always switched, so it does not support the idea that this crab will stay because the shell is familiar.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. It is too extreme and unsupported. The text says hermit crabs use shells for protection and that a growing crab must eventually find a larger shell, not that any crab would give up shells entirely.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. It contradicts the stated pattern. The researchers observed that crabs switched when a larger shell was nearby, and the text never says that a predator was involved in those switches.

question_text:
Archaeologists excavating a trading town on the Indian Ocean coast of East Africa found glass beads made in workshops in India. The beads were buried in layers dated to about 900 CE. Merchants at that time sailed between the two regions on seasonal monsoon winds, which blow toward Africa in one season and back toward India in another. Since the beads were made far from where they were found, the evidence suggests that ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: every town on the East African coast depended entirely on Indian goods for its survival.
answer_b: East African workshops had no skilled workers capable of making glass beads of their own.
answer_c: Indian merchants refused to sail to Africa during the season when winds blew toward India.
answer_d: the East African town and parts of India were in contact through sea trade around 900 CE.
explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it is supported by the facts in the text. The beads were made in India but found in an East African town, and merchants sailed between the two regions on monsoon winds, so the evidence suggests the regions were in contact through sea trade around 900 CE.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect because it is too extreme. Finding Indian beads in one town doesn't show that every coastal town depended entirely on Indian goods for survival.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect because it isn't supported by the text. The text says only that these beads came from India; it says nothing about whether East African workers could make glass beads.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect because it contradicts the text. The text says the winds blow back toward India in one season, which allowed merchants to sail between the two regions, not to refuse to sail.

question_text:
A lunar lander called Delphi-4 is designed to study a crater whose floor never receives direct sunlight. The lander's solar panels produce power only in direct sunlight, and its battery can run the instruments for about nine hours. Mission planners want the lander to collect data for at least three days. To meet that goal, the planners will most likely need to ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: land Delphi-4 where its panels receive direct sunlight each day.
answer_b: give the lander a power source that does not depend on sunlight.
answer_c: cancel the mission because no instrument can work on the crater floor.
answer_d: install stronger solar panels so the lander can charge on the crater floor.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer. The passage says the crater floor never gets direct sunlight, so the solar panels will not produce power there. It also says the battery lasts only about nine hours, far short of the three days planners want. Since neither stated power source can supply three days of power, the planners will need another source that works without sunlight.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. This contradicts the passage, which says the crater floor never receives direct sunlight. Landing the lander in sunlight would also mean it is no longer studying the crater floor.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. This is too extreme and is not supported. The passage says the battery can run the instruments for about nine hours, so instruments can work on the crater floor, just not for long enough.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. Stronger solar panels would not help, because the passage says panels produce power only in direct sunlight, and the crater floor never receives any.

question_text:
Lettuce is a cool-season crop. Its seeds germinate poorly when the soil stays warmer than about 80 degrees Fahrenheit, and plants that grow through long stretches of heat send up a flowering stalk and turn bitter. A gardener in a warm region plans to sow lettuce seed in mid-July, when soil temperatures there regularly top 85 degrees. Given these conditions, the gardener should expect that the July sowing will likely ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: produce few seedlings, and any plants that do grow may turn bitter.
answer_b: sprout more reliably than lettuce sown in cooler spring soil.
answer_c: fail completely, with not a single seed able to sprout.
answer_d: grow faster than spring lettuce and stay sweet through the summer.
explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The text says lettuce seeds germinate poorly in soil warmer than about 80 degrees and that plants grown through long heat turn bitter. Because July soil in the gardener's region regularly tops 85 degrees, it is logical to conclude that few seeds will sprout and that surviving plants may be bitter.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. The text says seeds germinate poorly in soil warmer than about 80 degrees, so sowing in hot July soil would make sprouting less reliable than in cool spring soil, not more reliable. This choice reverses the stated relationship.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. The text says seeds germinate poorly in warm soil, not that none can germinate. Claiming that not a single seed will sprout is too extreme to be supported by the passage.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. The text says plants grown through long stretches of heat turn bitter, which contradicts the claim that the lettuce will stay sweet. The passage also says nothing about lettuce growing faster in summer.

question_text:
Before the 1840s, painters stored oil paint in animal bladders, which were bulky and often leaked or dried out, so most artists mixed and used their paints inside a studio. Then the collapsible metal tube was introduced. It sealed paint airtight and fit easily into a small paint box. Because of these features, the invention most likely made it possible for painters to ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: spend more time working inside their studios than they had before.
answer_b: stop mixing colors by hand and never combine pigments again.
answer_c: carry their paints outdoors and finish landscape paintings on location.
answer_d: buy canvases at lower prices than they had paid in earlier decades.
explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The text says that bladder-stored paint was bulky and leaky, which kept most artists working in a studio. It then says the metal tube sealed paint airtight and fit into a small box, which removes both problems. It follows logically that painters could now carry paint outdoors and complete landscapes on location.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. This reverses the logic of the text. The tube solved the problems of carrying paint, so it would make it easier for painters to leave the studio, not keep them in it.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. The text says nothing about the tube changing how colors were mixed, and the claim that painters would never combine pigments again is too extreme to be supported.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. The text discusses how paint was stored and carried, not the price of canvases, so this detail is irrelevant and unsupported.

question_text:
Physiologists compared two groups of volunteers who each ran for 60 minutes in a warm room. One group drank water at regular intervals during the run, while the other group drank nothing. At the end of the hour, the runners who drank water had an average heart rate of 148 beats per minute, and the runners who drank nothing had an average heart rate of 162 beats per minute. These results suggest that, in this study, the runners who drank water ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: finished the hour with a higher average heart rate than the runners who drank nothing.
answer_b: finished the hour with about the same average heart rate as the runners who drank nothing.
answer_c: finished the hour with a lower average heart rate than the runners who drank nothing.
answer_d: finished the hour having run farther than the runners who drank nothing.
explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The text states that the runners who drank water had an average heart rate of 148 beats per minute at the end of the hour, while the runners who drank nothing had an average heart rate of 162 beats per minute. Because 148 is less than 162, the runners who drank water finished with a lower average heart rate.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. This choice reverses the comparison. The text gives 148 beats per minute for the water group and 162 beats per minute for the group that drank nothing, so the water group's average was lower, not higher.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. The text contradicts this choice. The two groups' average heart rates, 148 and 162 beats per minute, are different, so the groups did not finish with about the same average heart rate.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. This choice isn't supported by the text. Although the text says both groups ran for 60 minutes, it gives no information about how far either group ran, so it cannot be concluded that the water group covered more distance.

question_text:
In some desert towns, the air can pass 100 degrees Fahrenheit in the afternoon and fall below 50 degrees before dawn. Adobe, a brick made of dried mud and straw, takes in heat slowly and gives it off slowly. For centuries, builders in these towns have made house walls from adobe bricks stacked about a foot thick. Given these facts, it is likely that the builders chose thick adobe walls because they ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: protect houses from cold nights but make them hotter by day.
answer_b: cost far less to build than walls made of any other material.
answer_c: let the afternoon heat pass quickly into the rooms of a house.
answer_d: help keep indoor temperatures fairly steady despite large swings outside.
explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The text states that outdoor temperatures swing widely between afternoon and dawn and that adobe takes in and releases heat slowly. Thick adobe walls would therefore slow the movement of heat in and out of a house, which would keep indoor temperatures fairly steady.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. Because adobe takes in heat slowly, it would not make houses hotter by day, and a builder would not choose a material for that effect. This choice is not supported by the stated facts.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. The text gives no information about the cost of adobe or of other materials, and "any other material" is too extreme a claim to be supported.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. This contradicts the text, which states that adobe takes in heat slowly, so afternoon heat would not pass quickly into the rooms.

question_text:
Memory researchers have found that the timing of review matters. In one experiment, some students reviewed a list of vocabulary words three times on three separate days, while others reviewed the same list three times in a single evening. A month later, the students who had spread out their reviews remembered more words. Based on this finding, a student who wants to remember vocabulary for a test next month should probably ...

Which choice most logically completes the text?
answer_a: review the words in one long session on the night before the test.
answer_b: spread several review sessions across the days leading up to the test.
answer_c: review the words only once so that the information stays fresh.
answer_d: avoid reviewing the words until the week of the test.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer. The passage states that students who spread their reviews over separate days remembered more words a month later than students who reviewed the same number of times in one evening. A student who wants to remember vocabulary a month from now should therefore follow that approach and space out review sessions over several days.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. Reviewing everything in one long session is the approach that led to worse recall in the experiment, so the passage does not support recommending it.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. The passage compares different timings of three reviews each; it gives no evidence about reviewing only once, and nothing suggests a single review would help students remember more.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. The passage does not say that waiting to begin reviewing helps memory. Putting off all review until the week of the test would leave little room to spread out sessions, which is what the finding supports.
